# Erdos.p1055 — Erdős problem 1055

Reference: https://www.erdosproblems.com/1055
Imported from google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (`ErdosProblems/1055.lean`, theorem `erdos_1055`, AMS 11).

A prime $p$ is in class $1$ if the only prime divisors of $p+1$ are
$2$ or $3$. In general, a prime $p$ is in class $r$ if every prime factor
of $p+1$ is in some class $\leq r-1$, with equality for at least one prime factor.
Are there infinitely many primes in each class?

## Statement
∀ (r), {p | p.Prime ∧ IsOfClass r p}.Infinite

## Strategic notes
Open conjecture — prove-or-refute posture applies to sub-claims,
but the root asserts the conjectured statement itself. No
per-problem hints (benchmark integrity).
